title: Axiom
summary: An axiom is a declared starting statement or statement scheme of a formal theory.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal proof system context is fixed.

content.plain: An axiom is a declared starting statement or statement scheme of a formal theory.
content.exact: For a theory T in language L, Ax(T)⊆Sent(L) is the designated set or effectively described scheme of formulas usable without prior derivation.
content.example: A group theory presentation can take associativity as an axiom.
content.caveat: Axioms are conditional starting points, not self-certifying descriptions of physical reality.
